newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel shares suspended during debt talks.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel shares suspended during debt talks.

text.p: The stock of debt-ridden Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel were suspended Monday as it faced the latest crunch in its battle to restructure its $14 billion of debt.

Talks continued with the firm's leading creditors on restructuring its loans ahead of a midnight deadline for the ending of a mandate for two court-appointed mediators, a source close to the discussions said.
"The negotiations are advancing and the positions are getting closer," the source told Reuters.
"I can't say that there will be an agreement this evening because they are still negotiating. In any case, there is no breakdown," said the source, who declined to be identified.

The troubled Anglo-French company, set up in 1987, has been struggling to negotiate a restructuring of some 72 billion francs ($14 billion) of junior-ranked bank debt and interest since it froze payments to banks a year ago.

A spokesman for a Paris commercial court confirmed the mandate for mediators Robert Badinter and Lord Wakeham was due to expire at midnight Monday and said any statement would only be made after that.

Court president Jean-Pierre Mattei appointed the mediators in February to help negotiate the restructuring and extended their term in June and August. A source close to the talks said last week their mandate was not expected to be prolonged again.

Although the outline of a financial structure has been roughly agreed upon between Eurotunnel and its six leading lenders, they have been unable to agree on pricing of an expected debt-for-equity conversion and convertible securities that would lighten its loan payments.
The London Times newspaper reported 26 agent bank lenders of Eurotunnel would meet on Friday, Oct. 4, to look at latest proposals for dealing with the company's mountain of debt.
A Eurotunnel spokeswoman said it had asked for its shares to be suspended in Paris, London and Brussels to avoid speculation and the creation of a "false market" in the stock.
Eurotunnel had closed in Paris on Friday at 9.15 francs per share, compared with an all-time high of 120 francs and a 1987 flotation price of 35 francs.
